description: PROP-307c (specs/verification-architecture.md:518, restated verbatim at :1013-1017) is a required (tier:1, required:true, state.json PROP-117) proof obligation whose own text makes a blanket claim about ANY failure injected at step 9 of REQ-307's canonical call order: 'steps 7-9 ... use the existing buildChildSpec-based REQ-305 failure path; in every case, no row anywhere claims status:"active" for that child_id.' This round's own FIND-003 fix (the subject of this review) makes this claim independently falsifiable against the CURRENT, deliberately-implemented and tested code: step 9 is actually TWO sub-operations (spawn-orchestrator.mjs:698 the ledger 'active' append, then :700-736 the citizen-registry append). A failure in the SECOND sub-operation (citizens.json append, e.g. ENOTDIR) does NOT use 'the existing buildChildSpec-based REQ-305 failure path' at all -- it uses an entirely THIRD, new-this-round mechanism (pending-registry-append.js's durable queue), and the row DOES claim status:'active' (spawn-orchestrator.test.mjs:316, asserted directly: result.status === 'active' AND ledgerRows[0].status === 'active', both after the SAME injected step-9 failure PROP-307c says must never produce an active claim). This is REQUIRED behavior, not a bug -- it correctly implements REQ-305's own pre-existing Edge Case text (behavioral-spec.md:2559-2563: 'the ledger write ("active") succeeds but the SUBSEQUENT registry-append write fails for a transient reason ... THE SYSTEM SHALL retry the registry-append on the NEXT wake ... never a silent, permanent gap' -- explicitly describing an active-row-survives outcome for this exact step-9 sub-failure). The test file's own comment (spawn-orchestrator.test.mjs:309-311) implicitly concedes this tension by carving the transient registry-append case out as 'distinct from the step-9 ledger-append failure PROP-307c above already covers' -- but the ledger-append-itself failure ALSO does not fit PROP-307c's 'uses the buildChildSpec-based REQ-305 failure path' description: the code's own comment at spawn-orchestrator.mjs:697 says a raw ledger-append failure 'is allowed to propagate -- there is no lower-tier ledger left to record it in' (an uncaught rejection, not a buildChildSpec-based failure row either). So neither of step 9's two actual sub-failure modes matches PROP-307c's own governing description; the description was accurate only back when step 9 was a single monolithic operation with no registry-append-failure carve-out, and was never reconciled once REQ-305's own transient-retry edge case (which predates this fix) was actually implemented this round. This does not make the CONTRACT's own CRIT-203 wording wrong (CRIT-203, contracts/sprint-2.md:33, is narrower -- 'no row anywhere ever claims status:"active" for a FAILED ATTEMPT' -- and the FIND-003 case is not a failed attempt, executeSpawnAttempt resolves status:'active'), so CRIT-203 itself remains accurate and this is not a CRIT-203 violation. But PROP-307c is an artifact this same manifest lists for review (specs/verification-architecture.md), it is a required proof obligation that Phase 5 hardening must eventually mark 'proved', and its own current text will mislead whoever attempts that: either they wrongly conclude the FIND-003 code/tests violate PROP-307c (they don't -- REQ-305 itself requires this behavior), or they silently wave through an artifact whose own words contradict the governing requirement it cites. This needs a textual correction to PROP-307c (e.g. carving out the citizen-registry-append sub-case of step 9 the same way REQ-305's own Edge Cases already do) before Phase 5 can honestly evaluate it.
